A.explanation: Arrow to the right is radially away from X, which is the direction of the force on the negative test charge, not the direction of $E$ defined for a positive charge.

B.explanation: Arrow vertically up is perpendicular to the line XP, but the field of a point charge X at P must be radial along the line joining X and P.

C.explanation: Arrow to the left is radially toward X, which is opposite to the force on the negative test charge and so is the force direction on a positive test charge.

D.explanation: Arrow vertically down is perpendicular to the line XP, but the field of a point charge X at P must be radial along the line joining X and P.

hints: Notice P is to the right of X, so radially away from X at P means to the right, while radially toward X means to the left.
Recall electric field $E$ at a point is defined as the force per unit positive charge, $E = F/q$ with $q$ positive.
Connect the observation that a negative charge at P is pushed to the right to what would happen to a positive charge placed at P.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: charge X is on the left and point P is on the right, so the line XP is horizontal.
State the observation: a negatively charged test charge at P feels a repulsive force radially away from X, so that force points horizontally to the right.
State the defining rule: electric field direction at P is the direction of the force that a small positive test charge would feel at P, given by $E = F/q$.
Infer the sign of X: since it repels a negative charge, X itself must be negative, so a positive charge at P would be attracted toward X.
Therefore the field at P due to X points horizontally to the left, toward the negative charge X. This is option C.
